description: Use this first when the user names a person (a name with a company or domain, a LinkedIn URL or an email) or a company and wants contact details, a profile or firmographics, such as the email of a founder at a given company. One call runs the provider waterfall. Use it, not people_company_search, whenever you have a name with a company or domain, a LinkedIn URL or an email. Give people (name with company or domain, LinkedIn URL, email or phone) or companies (domain, name or LinkedIn URL), up to 10 records per call. Each requested field runs a waterfall by default: Firecrawl tries the providers that can use your inputs one at a time, ordered by listed price, and stops as soon as the field is found. Without contact_fields a person gets a profile and a company gets firmographics; with contact_fields (work_email, personal_email, mobile) each person gets those values and, unless profile is false, the profile in the same call. Ask for mobile only when the task needs a phone number; it is the costliest field and nothing is spent on it otherwise. A work email is on the company domain when one is known and never on a known free-mail domain or a known role mailbox; fields says for each answer which provider gave it, whether the email was verified and whether its domain matched. Set verified_only to get only verified emails. Each result is the provider's raw response, tagged with the provider. A provider that finds the value is charged its listed price; misses are free. max_credits caps the call; without it the call is uncapped. To call one specific provider, use alexandria_library_read instead. Example: {"contact_fields":["work_email"],"people":[{"name":"Jane Doe","domain":"example.com"}]}.

contact_fields.description: People only. Find these contact values for each person; companies in the same call still get firmographics. Include mobile only when a phone number is needed: phone lookups are the costliest and run, and bill, only when mobile is listed.

max_credits.description: Most credits the whole call may spend. Set it only to a budget the user gave; left out, the call has no cap. A provider is tried only while its listed price still fits, so 0 runs nothing paid.

objective.description: The user's underlying goal for this call, in one sentence: what they are ultimately trying to accomplish, not a restatement of the URL or query. Reuse it across related calls. Avoid sensitive information.

people.description: People to enrich. People and companies together are at most 10 per call.

email.description: Any email known for the person.

phone.description: Any phone number known for the person.

profile.description: With contact_fields, also return each person's profile in the same call, looked up first so the contact lookups can use it. Default true; false skips it.

verified_only.description: Email fields: return only an address the provider verified as deliverable. Default false returns the best address found, with fields.<field>.verified saying whether it was verified.

name: people_company_enrich
